what_was_done.action: AC 1: Extended buildCoherenceEscalationRule's matches() with path (b). For each unique epicId in events: read snapshot, short-circuit on hasRecentCoherenceDispatch (cross-rule dedup via stage-dispatched(run-coherence-agent) events), then evaluate path (a) (review:needs-human) OR path (b) (latest marker → interpretMarkerForRouting → nextAgent=coherence). Path (b) discovers latestAgentExitedFor() to find the most recent agent-exited event's stage, builds markerId=<epicId>-<stage>, calls injected readMarker, calls interpretMarkerForRouting; only enqueues a match when override=true AND nextAgent=coherence.
what_was_done.result: Both paths produce ReconcilerMatch objects with rule-name-prefixed idempotency keys (coherence-escalation::<epicId>::<stage>). Path (a) preserved bit-for-bit when readMarker is undefined (back-compat). Path (a) and path (b) are mutually exclusive per epic per tick (path a wins via continue) — single dispatch per epic per tick.

what_was_done.action: AC 4: Idempotency key includes (epicId, stage) per ADR-009. Verified two named tests: 'idempotency — same (epicId, stage) within horizon does NOT refire' (single dispatch across two ticks) AND 'idempotency — stage transition (builder→reviewer) allows refire' (different markers for different stages produce two dispatches because the key changes).
what_was_done.result: Both tests pass. The stage-transition test verifies that a builder-marker dispatch followed by a reviewer-marker dispatch produces 2 fetch calls (different idempotency keys). The same-stage test verifies a single dispatch across two ticks (same idempotency key consumed on first tick).

what_was_done.action: AC 5: Cross-rule dedup with marker-driven-routing. Two named tests. (1) 'cross-rule dedup — both rules on same marker each fire once (different rule-name prefix)' registers BOTH rules in a single Reconciler, sees marker status=needs-decision, expects 2 dispatches in tick 1 (one per rule, different idempotency keys), then 0 dispatches on tick 2 (each rule's reconciler-action-taken event blocks its own re-fire). (2) 'idempotency keys are rule-scoped — marker-driven-routing's prior action does NOT block coherence-escalation' pre-seeds a reconciler-action-taken event from marker-driven-routing and verifies coherence-escalation still fires (proves the rule-name prefix in keys prevents collision).
what_was_done.result: Both tests pass. Confirms reconciler core's (rule-name, idempotencyKey) dedup works as documented; the rule-name prefix in path (b)'s key (coherence-escalation::) is the load-bearing element preventing accidental cross-rule dedup.

what_was_done.action: AC 8: Orchestrator-down behaviour verified. Test 'AC 8: orchestrator HTTP failure throws (reconciler retries next tick)' mocks fetch to return HTTP 500. The rule's act() throws (preserved zsjv hotfix behaviour: HTTP non-2xx → Error). The reconciler core swallows the error per its always-emit reconciler-action-taken contract; this consumes the idempotency bucket for the horizon, which is the documented 'logs and retries when bucket rotates' behaviour. No operator escalation from inside the rule (per ADR-008).

No path (b) cross-fall to operator routing happens — coherence is the universal handler for routing failures including orchestrator-down per ADR-008 (already enforced via wlsr.18 BLOCKER_CLASS_TO_AGENT['orchestrator-down']='coherence').

surprises_or_findings: (1) Existing legacy test file at __tests__/lib/coherence-escalation.test.ts uses a snap() helper that does NOT include currentStage. To preserve existing tests without modification (AC 2), I made currentStage OPTIONAL on the EpicSnapshot interface. Path (a)'s idempotency key falls back to a synthetic 'needs-human' stage when currentStage is absent — keeps the key well-defined per ADR-009 even in the legacy snapshot shape. (2) Cross-rule dedup test initially used status=failure marker but marker-driven-routing's hasRoutingIntent check requires next_agent set OR status=needs-decision. Switched to status=needs-decision so BOTH rules fire — this is the intended cross-rule scenario for AC 5 verification. (3) Bootstrap's lone lint warning at line 598 (require('fs') style import in hs5 fallback code) is pre-existing on main; verified by the warning being in untouched code. (4) The legacy rule's idempotency key was 'coherence-escalation::<epicId>' (no stage); the new key adds stage. This is technically a key-shape change for path (a) — legacy reconciler-action-taken events on the OLD key will not match the new key. In production, this means a single one-time dispatch may fire for any epic that had a path-(a) dispatch on the old key BEFORE wlsr.7 lands; subsequent dispatches use the new keyed shape. Considered acceptable: idempotency horizon is 1 hour; the behaviour change is observed at most once per epic at the deployment boundary; coherence is idempotent at the agent level (re-dispatching coherence on the same epic is benign — it reads the journal and either dispatches the same action again or escalates). (5) Per-AC checkpoint table NOT written this build (Wave 2 builder for this rule operates on a self-contained scope; mid-build crash recovery would not lose substantial work).
